---
title: "Combining with external data: school locations (DUO)"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 7,
  fig.height = 6,
  fig.align = "center",
  out.width = "100%"
)
```

PDOK is rarely the only source you need. A common pattern is to take a table
from another open API, turn it into spatial data, and combine it with
authoritative PDOK geometry. This article does that with
[DUO](https://duo.nl/)'s open data on schools. It shows that combining sources
often means a little data wrangling first, and that an external table with BAG
ids pairs naturally with a server-side `filter` on the BAG.

```{r setup}
library(pdokr)
library(tmap)
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(httr2)
```

DUO publishes its data through a [CKAN open-data
API](https://onderwijsdata.duo.nl/). Every table is one resource. Some are large,
so this helper fetches one in pages, letting `httr2` retry a request that drops
or that the DUO server answers with a temporary gateway error.

```{r helper}
read_duo <- function(resource_id, page_size = 5000) {
  pages <- list()
  offset <- 0
  repeat {
    resp <- request("https://onderwijsdata.duo.nl/api/3/action/datastore_search") |>
      req_url_query(resource_id = resource_id, limit = page_size, offset = offset) |>
      req_retry(
        max_tries = 6, backoff = ~ 5,
        is_transient = ~ resp_status(.x) %in% c(429, 502, 503, 504)
      ) |>
      req_perform() |>
      resp_body_json(simplifyVector = TRUE)
    page <- resp$result$records
    if (length(page) == 0) break
    pages[[length(pages) + 1]] <- page
    if (nrow(page) < page_size) break
    offset <- offset + page_size
  }
  do.call(rbind, pages)
}
```

## Fetch the education locations

The `onderwijslocaties` resource lists every location where education *may* take
place, each with coordinates and a `BAG_ID`: the identifier of the BAG
*verblijfsobject* (unit of use) the location occupies.

```{r locations}
locations <- read_duo("a7e3f323-6e46-4dca-a834-369d9d520aa8")
nrow(locations)
```

There is a catch: these are *possible* education locations, not recognized
schools. A conference center that hosts the odd exam, or a commercial training
firm, is in here too. Mapping them straight away would put dots where no school
exists.

## Keep only the recognized schools

To find the schools recognized in law we combine two more DUO tables. The
`relaties...` resource links a location (`ONDERWIJSLOCATIECODE`) to a recognized
institution (`VESTIGINGSCODE`); the `vestigingserkenningen` resource describes
that institution — its name and the education law it falls under (`WET`). Both
tables are historical, so a row counts only when it has no `EINDDATUM`.

```{r join}
relations    <- read_duo("c18ec7dd-aa4e-4b51-997c-782955f1aa38")
institutions <- read_duo("01fd2a5f-40af-456f-864d-13265a51e5e2")

# translate the education-law code into a readable sector
sectors <- c(WPO = "Primary", WVO = "Secondary", WEC = "Special",
             WEB = "Vocational (MBO)", WHW = "Higher education")

# current institutions (no end date), one row each, with a readable sector
institutions <- institutions |>
  filter(is.na(EINDDATUM)) |>
  distinct(VESTIGINGSCODE, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  mutate(sector = unname(sectors[WET])) |>
  select(VESTIGINGSCODE, sector, school = VOLLEDIGE_NAAM)

# current location -> recognized institution, one institution per location
link <- relations |>
  filter(is.na(EINDDATUM)) |>
  select(ONDERWIJSLOCATIECODE, VESTIGINGSCODE) |>
  inner_join(institutions, by = "VESTIGINGSCODE") |>
  distinct(ONDERWIJSLOCATIECODE, .keep_all = TRUE)

# inner join drops every location without a recognized institution
schools <- inner_join(locations, link, by = "ONDERWIJSLOCATIECODE")
nrow(schools)
count(schools, sector)
```

Only the locations backed by a recognized institution remain — no training
venues, no exam halls — and each carries its school name and education sector.

One quirk worth knowing: a university or college is registered as a *single*
recognized institution, so only its official location appears here, not its
every building. The map below is therefore dominated by primary and secondary
schools, which register each site.

## Link the schools to the BAG

Each DUO location carries GPS coordinates, but it also carries something
better: a `BAG_ID`. That id points straight at the BAG `verblijfsobject`, so
instead of trusting DUO's coordinates we can fetch the authoritative BAG
position of every school with a server-side filter (see [Filtering data by
attribute](filtering-by-attribute.html)).

The ids are nationwide, so we first narrow down to the city of Utrecht with
DUO's own place name. That leaves a modest list of ids for `%in%`; had there
been thousands, `pdok_where()` would send them in batches of 300 and
`pdok_read()` would combine the results just the same. We also drop the
locations without a BAG id: a missing value cannot be matched by the server,
so `pdok_where()` refuses a vector that holds one. (DUO's table also carries
a few hundred ids that are not 16-digit BAG ids at all; those simply match
nothing.)

```{r bag-ids}
ids <- schools |>
  filter(PLAATSNAAM == "Utrecht", !is.na(BAG_ID)) |>
  pull(BAG_ID)
length(ids)

units <- pdok_read(
  "kadaster/bag", "verblijfsobject",
  filter = pdok_where(identificatie %in% ids)
)
nrow(units)
```

The result is one BAG point per school, in the BAG's own coordinates. A join
on the id brings the school name and sector across (row order follows the
service, so join rather than bind):

```{r join-bag}
utrecht_schools <- units |>
  inner_join(
    select(schools, BAG_ID, school, sector, STRAATNAAM),
    by = c(identificatie = "BAG_ID")
  )
utrecht_schools |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  count(sector)
```

For the maps we also want the municipal boundary and its districts from CBS.

```{r boundary}
gemeenten <- pdok_read(
  "cbs/gebiedsindelingen", "gemeente_gegeneraliseerd", datetime = 2025
)
utrecht <- filter(gemeenten, statnaam == "Utrecht")
```

```{r map-overview}
tmap_mode("plot")

tm_shape(utrecht) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "grey95", col = "grey60") +
  tm_shape(utrecht_schools) +
  tm_dots(
    fill = "sector", size = 0.5,
    fill.scale = tm_scale_categorical(values = "brewer.set2"),
    fill.legend = tm_legend("Sector")
  ) +
  tm_title("Recognized schools in Utrecht, by sector")
```

## Map the school buildings

Each school sits in a building from the BAG, and the BAG tells us which one:
every `verblijfsobject` carries a `pand.href` column linking to its building.
`pdok_read_href()` follows those links. It reads each linked building once,
one small request each, so nothing else is downloaded, and attaches it to
the school that links to it. Think of it as a join: the result is the schools
table with the building's columns alongside and the building footprint as
its geometry. We cannot use `pdok_where()` here as we did for the units: a
`verblijfsobject` does not carry its building's `identificatie`, only the
link, and the id in the link is internal to the server. Following the link
is the only way across. This scales to any list: all schools in the Netherlands are
roughly 9,000 links, which take about a quarter of an hour at the default,
deliberately modest request rate.

```{r buildings}
school_buildings <- pdok_read_href(utrecht_schools, "pand")
nrow(school_buildings)
```

A few schools share a building and a few occupy two, so the row count
differs slightly from the number of schools. Columns that both BAG layers
have, such as `identificatie`, carry the `pand.` prefix on the building side:

```{r peek-buildings}
select(school_buildings, school, pand.identificatie, bouwjaar) |>
  head(3)
```

For the map we zoom in on the historic center, using the CBS districts:

```{r footprints}
wijken <- pdok_read(
  "cbs/gebiedsindelingen", "wijk_gegeneraliseerd", datetime = 2025,
  filter_by = utrecht, predicate = "within"
)
binnenstad <- filter(wijken, grepl("Binnenstad", statnaam))
center_buildings <- pdok_filter_by(school_buildings, binnenstad)
nrow(center_buildings)
```

The result is real school buildings, colored by sector. Click one for the
school that uses it.

```{r map-interactive}
tmap_mode("view")

tm_basemap(pdok_basemap("grijs")) +
  tm_shape(center_buildings) +
  tm_polygons(
    fill = "sector",
    fill.scale = tm_scale_categorical(values = "brewer.set2"),
    fill.legend = tm_legend("Sector"),
    col = "grey30", lwd = 0.5, id = "school",
    popup = tm_popup(vars = c("School" = "school", "Sector" = "sector",
                              "Street" = "STRAATNAAM"))
  ) +
  tm_credits("Kaartgegevens © Kadaster")
```

```{r reset, include = FALSE}
tmap_mode("plot")
```
